subject: Communication
title: Contempt: The Relationship Killer Expression
description: A 60-second lesson on Contempt: The Relationship Killer Expression.

hook.text: John Gottman can predict divorce with 93% accuracy by watching one facial expression: contempt.

buildup.text: Contempt is a unilateral lip raise — one corner of the mouth pulled up. It signals moral superiority.

discovery.text: Unlike anger (which says 'I disagree'), contempt says 'I'm better than you.' It destroys respect.

twist.text: Contempt is the only asymmetrical universal expression — it appears on just one side of the face.

climax.text: In relationships, contempt predicts failure more than any other emotion — including anger or sadness.

punchline.text: The deadliest expression isn't rage. It's a half-smile.

quiz.question: Who uses contempt to predict divorce with 93% accuracy?

details.summary: Contempt is displayed as a unilateral lip raise on one side of the face. John Gottman identified it as the single strongest predictor of relationship dissolution, more damaging than anger or criticism.
details.whyItMatters: Recognizing contempt early in communication allows intervention before it corrodes trust and respect in personal and professional relationships.
takeaways: Contempt shows as a one-sided mouth raise or smirk
Gottman found it predicts divorce with high accuracy
It signals superiority and a fundamental lack of respect

faq.question: Why is contempt more destructive than anger?
faq.answer: Anger treats the other person as an equal who has done something wrong. Contempt treats them as beneath consideration. This fundamental disrespect corrodes the foundation of mutual regard that relationships require to survive.

faq.question: How can couples address contempt when it appears?
faq.answer: Gottman recommends building a culture of appreciation to counteract contempt. Expressing genuine admiration and gratitude regularly creates a buffer. When contempt appears, addressing the underlying resentment directly is essential for repair.
